reason: E1 directly supports that electronegativity and mass differences drive local chemical fluctuations and induce strain, but it does not provide evidence that these strain fields inhibit diffusion or phase segregation, nor does it address nanoparticle stability across the specified temperature range.
premises: Electronegativity and mass differences are the primary drivers of local chemical fluctuations in high-entropy materials.
Local chemical fluctuations create heterogeneous lattice strain fields.
These strain fields inhibit rapid elemental diffusion and phase segregation.
This stabilization mechanism operates across 473–1923 K in nanoparticles.
